title: Feedback Control for Multi-Objective Graph Self-Supervision
abstract: arXiv:2602.05036v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Can multi-task self-supervised learning on graphs be coordinated without the usual tug-of-war between objectives? Graph self-supervised learning (SSL) offers a growing toolbox of pretext objectives like mutual information, reconstruction, and contrastive learning, yet combining them reliably remains challenging due to objective interference and training instability. Most multi-pretext pipelines use per-update mixing, forcing every parameter update to be a compromise and leading to three failure modes: Disagreement (conflict-induced negative transfer), Drift (nonstationary objective utility), and Drought (hidden starvation of underserved objectives). We argue that coordination is fundamentally a temporal allocation problem: deciding when each objective receives optimization budget, not merely how to weigh them. translated_title: 面向多目标图自监督学习的反馈控制
translated_abstract: 图上的多任务自监督学习能否在没有目标之间常见拉锯战的情况下实现协调？图自监督学习（SSL）提供了日益丰富的前置任务目标工具箱，如互信息、重建和对比学习，然而由于目标干扰和训练不稳定性，可靠地组合这些目标仍然充满挑战。大多数多前置任务流程采用每次更新混合的方式，迫使每一次参数更新都成为一种妥协，并导致三种失败模式：分歧（冲突引起的负迁移）、漂移（目标效用的非平稳性）和干涸（被忽视目标的隐性饥饿）。我们认为，协调本质上是一个时间分配问题：决定每个目标何时获得优化预算，而不仅仅是如何对它们进行加权。我们提出了ControlG，一个控制理论框架，将多目标图SSL重新构建为反馈控制的时间分配问题（摘要在此处被截断）。
tldr: 该论文提出ControlG框架，将多目标图自监督学习中的目标协调重新表述为反馈控制的时间分配问题，通过控制论方法解决传统混合方式导致的目标干扰与训练不稳定问题。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces ControlG, a control-theoretic framework that recasts multi-objective graph self-supervised learning as a feedback-controlled temporal allocation problem, addressing objective interference and training instability through control theory.
